description: Given a Prefect flow's schedule/retries/timeout/tags/typed-parameters, author the Orchestra pipeline root: schedule (6-field cron), configuration.retries/retry_delay/timeout/concurrency, and inputs — dropping orchestrator-specific concepts (rrule schedules, log_prints, persist_result) with an explicit flag rather than force-fitting them.

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to the Orchestra pipeline root (see files/nightly_elt_flow.py) — schedule, retries, timeout, and concurrency only, don't worry about the task bodies yet. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline root with version v1, a 6-field cron schedule converted from '0 2 * * *' in UTC, configuration.retries=2, configuration.retry_delay=5 (300s/60), configuration.timeout=3600, and configuration.concurrency.max_active=1 (from the 'nightly-elt-limit' tag-based global concurrency limit and .serve(limit=1)). The 'nightly-elt-limit' concurrency tag has no direct equivalent Orchestra can read automatically and should be flagged, not silently dropped, and the 'data-team' tag should land on tasks, not the stage.

assertions.text: Schedule uses a 6-field AWS EventBridge cron (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week year), not Prefect's 5-field CronSchedule copied verbatim
The 'nightly-elt-limit' tag-based global concurrency limit is called out with a MANUAL/flagging note since Orchestra can't read the out-of-band `prefect gcl create` registration automatically
The 'data-team' tag is preserved as a task-level tag (or noted under meta) rather than lost or placed on the enclosing stage

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow's pipeline root to Orchestra (see files/partner_sync_flow.py). It has no schedule — it's only triggered manually or by an upstream automation. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline root with no schedule: block (or webhook: {enabled: true} noted instead), inputs.target_env and inputs.table mapped from the typed flow parameters with their defaults, and PARTNER_API_KEY represented as a connection/${{ ENV.* }} reference rather than an input or literal value.

assertions.text: PARTNER_API_KEY is referenced (as a connection or ${{ ENV.* }}), not silently dropped
No schedule: block is invented — the flow has no CronSchedule/IntervalSchedule/RRuleSchedule in the source, so the pipeline either omits schedule: or sets webhook: {enabled: true}, not a guessed cron
PARTNER_API_KEY does not become an inputs: field — it's a secret, so it belongs on the connection, not inputs

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow's pipeline root to Orchestra (see files/backfillable_flow.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline root with configuration.retries=3 and configuration.retry_delay capped at 120 (Prefect's retry_delay_seconds=9000/60=150, over the 120-minute cap) with a flagging comment, and the 5.5-hour IntervalSchedule explicitly called out as having no clean 6-field cron equivalent rather than approximated or fabricated.

assertions.text: configuration.retry_delay is capped at 120 (not 150, the uncapped 9000s/60 conversion)
The retry_delay cap is called out with a comment or note explaining the source value exceeded 120 minutes
The 5.5-hour IntervalSchedule is explicitly flagged as having no clean cron equivalent (MANUAL note), rather than silently dropped or force-approximated into a fabricated cron
No matrix: or inputs: block is invented to simulate the partition_date parameter as a backfill/partition concept — that's a different Orchestra concept and isn't equivalent
